settings.heading: Our Story
settings.body:
40 Onzas was born from a refusal — a refusal to renderize, to mass produce, to sand the edges off what makes an object alive. Each piece begins in the atelier as raw metal and stubborn intention.

We work the way the old houses worked: by hand, by eye, by feel. Silver, gold and bronze are cut, hammered and finished until the material itself decides it is done.

The workshop smells of wax and flame. Tools older than the hands that hold them line the benches. Nothing here is rushed — a single ring may pass through fire a dozen times before it earns its finish.

Imperfection is not corrected; it is kept. It is the fingerprint of the maker, the proof that a person, not a machine, stood behind the work.
Time invested is value. A piece from 40 Onzas is not a product — it is a record of hours, of decisions, of a dialogue between maker and material that can never be repeated.
